findings.evidence: "Without a structured-question tool, ask in plain conversation: number the options, accept several numbers where a step says `multiSelect: true`, and wait for the answer."
findings.fix: Keep the non-obvious rule ('Never answer a question on the user's behalf because no tool exists for it') and shorten the generic part about numbering options to one clause. The model produces numbered plain-text questions without being told, so record the shortened wording as a removal.

findings.evidence: "`references/wizard-flow.md` sets the question order (Step 2.2); Steps 2.3 to 2.8 hold the per-topic rules it points to." The order lives in a reference, but Steps 2.3 to 2.8 come after it in the body, so the reader has to switch back and forth between the two files.
findings.fix: Add one line to the start of Step 2 saying that Steps 2.3 to 2.8 are lookups that wizard-flow.md steps 5 to 11 call, not steps to run in body order. For example: 'Do not run 2.3 to 2.8 top to bottom; enter each one only when wizard-flow.md names it.'

findings.evidence: "Never skip announcing the target path before asking reviewer questions — user must know where config is headed from the start."
findings.fix: Replace the generic reason with the failure it prevents. For example: 'otherwise an owner who answers ten lane questions for the project can find that the run wrote over the global roster used by every project.'

findings.evidence: The description is 1013 of 1024 characters and spends about 250 characters on internal mechanics ('Detects installed CLIs and models, proposes a review set and an execute set from the model catalog for the owner to pick, asks each role's order, effort and opt-in flags'), so almost no room is left for later trigger changes.
findings.fix: Sets up, refreshes or checks ai-kit's cross-AI lanes: which models review plans, which implement them, and each role's fallback order. Picks lanes with the owner from installed CLIs and the model catalog, then writes the [lanes] table of ./.aikit/config.toml (or the user config.toml with --global) and asks before it replaces an existing roster. Use when the user wants cross-AI review or execute lanes set up, refreshed or checked, wants a second-opinion reviewer or a fallback implementer, even without the word lanes; when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers it because no lanes exist; to find lane providers opencode no longer lists; or to migrate an old review-spec.toml. Supports --check-only (availability report, no config writes), --local and --global (pick the target, never consent to replace it). Not for running a review or execute with configured lanes, hand-editing one lane value, or editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.

findings.evidence: "How a stored pair is run, waited for and retried is in [`../ai-kit-cross-ai/SKILL.md`](../ai-kit-cross-ai/SKILL.md) for runtime/model dispatch; this skill only stores the pair." This sibling-skill reference sits outside the skill root and has no load condition.
findings.fix: Add a condition such as 'Read it only when the owner asks how a stored lane is dispatched or retried; do NOT load it during a normal setup run.' Keep the link.

findings.evidence: There are 12 should-trigger and 10 should-not-trigger queries. Two positives were appended after the negatives (lines 20-21). Only one positive is casual (line 21), and none has a file path or other personal context.
